newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-MADDUX AND BRAVES STOP CARDINALS TO FORCE SEVEN GAME.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MADDUX AND BRAVES STOP CARDINALS TO FORCE SEVEN GAME.

text.p: Four-time Cy Young Award winner Greg Maddux held the St Louis Cardinals to one run as the Atlanta Braves forced a seventh and deciding game in the National League Championship Series with a 3-1 victory on Wednesday.
Maddux and reliever Mark Wholers combined on a six-hitter to turn the series into a one-game, winner goes to the World Series showdown.
For the second consecutive game, the defending world champions staved off elimination as Atlanta's vaunted pitching staff shut down the St Louis attack.
Maddux shook off his Game 2 loss, allowing four hits and striking out seven without a walk through seven shutout innings before tiring in the eighth, when the Cardinals managed their lone run.
"I knew he was going to be tremendous tonight," Atlanta catcher Javy Lopez said of Maddux, who displayed the form that saw him named the National League's best pitcher the last four years.
"I was concentrating on trying to catch that shutout," Lopez said. "I couldn't but at least we won, that's all that counts."

Two nights after exploding for 22 hits in a 14-0 rout, the Braves scratched out single runs in the second and fifth innings before adding an insurance run in the eighth against surprise rookie starter Alan Benes and three relievers.

In Game 7 Thursday night in Atlanta, the Braves' Tom Glavine will go against the Cardinals' Donovan Osborne in a battle of left-handers to decide who faces the American League champion New York Yankees in the World Series.
